name: No-Code Supply Co.
tagline: Hand-picked daily directory of design, no-code and AI resources
description: A long-running, human-curated directory of roughly 3,000 designer, developer and AI resources, split into Inspo, Code, Learn, Tools, Shop and Creators. Every entry is dated and cross-tagged by type (Website, App, Utility, Snippet, Video, Directory, Library), by ~100 topic tags and by ~60 industries, so you can filter to Webflow GSAP portfolios or MCP/Skill tooling in two clicks. The house also ships its own products (MAST, a CSS framework for Webflow and Sanity), a podcast called Restock, and a shop that resells vetted third-party courses, icon sets and UI kits. Aimed at Webflow/Framer-leaning designers and no-code builders who want a taste filter rather than an algorithm.
pricing_detail: Directory is free. Shop mixes own digital goods (Simple Project Manager Template $10) with resold third-party goods (Untitled UI $119, Typography in web design course EUR 399, Tambien Course EUR 195, central icon system $59, Ultimate Notion Icons $49, Koala UI EUR 119+, Osmo EUR 25/mo, Relume Library $32/mo).
agent_guidance: Reach for this when you need a taste-checked shortlist of no-code/Webflow tooling or a real human-picked example of a marketing site, not when you need code you can install. Its whole catalogue is server-rendered in the homepage HTML, so a single fetch plus a tag filter gets you further than crawling item pages one by one. It ranks nothing and exposes no API or feed, so treat it as a discovery surface and always verify a linked tool separately before you recommend it.
why_it_matters: One of the few design directories with an actual editorial point of view rather than SEO-driven bulk, and it stays current — new entries dated within the last week. The Webflow/Framer/no-code slant makes it complementary to code-first indexes rather than duplicative.
notable_for: own products: MAST CSS framework, Restock podcast
shop of vetted third-party design goods
evidence: https://www.nocodesupply.co/ (WebFetch + raw curl of 748KB HTML, full tag/type/industry lists read verbatim), https://www.nocodesupply.co/shop (WebFetch). /library 404s.

name: Shapefest
description: A single-author library of over 100,000 photoreal 3D renders made by Joseph Todaro in Cinema 4D, all shot with the same lighting, camera angles and transparent alpha so anything you mix stays visually coherent. It is organised into four material collections (Clay, Plastic, Glass, Metal) with per-colour sub-collections, plus shape packs such as 3000 Hands, Floating Blobs, Isometric Building Blocks, CryptoFluffs and Isometric Material Icons. Free downloads are capped at 512x512 px, which is enough for icons and small UI illustration; 3000x3000 px needs All Access. Best for designers who want spot 3D illustration for a landing page or deck without opening a 3D app.

pricing_detail: Free packs at 512x512 px. All Access: $20/month or $299 lifetime, covering 500+ packs at 3000x3000 px with a Pro License and one-click downloads. Extended License available for including shapes in a UI kit as design elements.
agent_guidance: Use this when a marketing page or deck needs one hero 3D object and you want a rendered PNG rather than a WebGL scene — it is far cheaper than shipping three.js for a decorative shape. Pick everything within one material collection (all Frosted Glass, or all Black Clay) so the lighting and camera match; mixing Clay with Neon Glass looks like stock. Be aware the free tier is 512x512, which will look soft on a 2x hero, and the licence forbids redistribution — never bundle the PNGs into a template or repo you hand back to the user.
why_it_matters: The largest single-authored, visually consistent 3D asset library on the open web, and the consistency is what makes it usable — most 3D stock falls apart the moment you place two assets side by side.
notable_for: 100,000+ renders, one author, one lighting rig
four material families: clay, plastic, glass, metal
true alpha transparency on every PNG

name: Heroicons
tagline: 324 MIT SVG icons in four sizes, from the Tailwind CSS team
description: The Tailwind Labs icon set: 324 icons drawn at 24x24 outline (1.5px stroke) and 24x24 solid, plus a 324-icon 20x20 Mini solid set and a 316-icon 16x16 Micro solid set — 1,288 SVGs in total, all MIT licensed. Ships as raw SVG files, as React components (@heroicons/react) and as Vue components (@heroicons/vue), so you import a named component rather than pasting markup. The site lets you copy an icon as SVG or as JSX directly. For anyone building with Tailwind, this is the default icon layer.
agent_guidance: Default to Heroicons when the project already uses Tailwind — the sizes and 1.5px stroke are tuned to Tailwind's spacing scale, so icons optically match text without hand-fiddling. Import the size-specific path (@heroicons/react/24/outline, /20/solid, /16/solid) rather than a barrel import, or you pull the whole 1,288-file set into the bundle. Reach for Lucide instead when you need breadth (Heroicons is deliberately small at 324 concepts) or a stroke width you can vary; reach for Phosphor when you need multiple weights of the same glyph.
why_it_matters: The de facto icon set of the Tailwind ecosystem: small, opinionated, MIT, and drawn by the same people who set the spacing scale you are already using, so it never fights the layout.
notable_for: copy as SVG or JSX from the site
evidence: https://heroicons.com/ (WebFetch), https://github.com/tailwindlabs/heroicons (WebFetch + GitHub API for stars/licence/pushed_at), jsDelivr flat file listing for heroicons@2.2.0 (exact per-variant SVG counts: 324/324/324/316). Latest tagged release v2.2.0, 2024-11-18; repo last pushed 2026-05-12.

name: FigComponents
tagline: 1,619 copy-paste Figma components, 1,002 of them free, CC BY 4.0
description: A web catalogue of 1,619 Figma components — 1,002 free and 670 pro — that you copy to the clipboard from the browser and paste straight into a Figma file, with no plugin to install. Coverage is broadest on web marketing and app UI: 979 Website, 723 Section, 524 Landing Page, 319 iPhone, 299 Mobile App/iOS, 213 Dark, 204 Untitled UI, 137 Dashboard, plus long tails for tables, charts, auth, ecommerce, crypto/NFT and wireframes. Everything is CC BY 4.0, so it is usable commercially with attribution. Built by Danny Postma; useful as a fast source of Figma reference blocks rather than as a maintained design system.
pricing_detail: 1,002 components free, 670 marked Pro. No price shown on the public catalogue pages; Pro items are gated behind an account.
agent_guidance: This is Figma-only — it produces no code, so never suggest it when the user wants something installable; send them to a shadcn registry instead. Its real use is giving a designer a paste-ready starting frame for a landing page or dashboard, and its 204 Untitled UI components make it a cheap way to sample that system before buying it. Check the freshness before you lean on it: the static build served in August 2026 was compiled in November 2024, so treat the catalogue as a frozen archive rather than a growing library, and confirm the CC BY 4.0 attribution requirement is acceptable for commercial work.
why_it_matters: One of the few large Figma component collections that is genuinely free and openly licensed rather than a lead magnet, and the copy-to-clipboard flow removes the usual community-file duplication step.
notable_for: copy to clipboard, no Figma plugin
static build appears frozen since Nov 2024

name: Headless UI
tagline: 16 unstyled, fully accessible React and Vue primitives from Tailwind Labs
description: Tailwind Labs' primitive library: 16 completely unstyled components that ship the hard parts — keyboard interaction, ARIA wiring, focus trapping, scroll locking and inert backgrounds — and none of the visual design. Documented components are Button, Checkbox, Combobox, Dialog, Disclosure, Dropdown Menu, Fieldset, Input, Listbox, Popover, Radio Group, Select, Switch, Tabs, Textarea and Transition, each exposing state through data attributes (data-active, data-focus, data-disabled, data-open) and render props so you style with plain Tailwind classes. Available as @headlessui/react and @headlessui/vue, both MIT. For teams that want Tailwind-native interaction primitives without adopting a whole design system.
agent_guidance: Prefer Headless UI over Radix when the project is Tailwind-first and you want to style states with data-attribute variants (data-open:rotate-180) instead of a separate CSS layer — the API surface is much smaller and there is nothing to configure. Prefer Radix when you need components Headless UI simply does not ship: tooltip, hover card, accordion, slider, toast, context menu, navigation menu, or a scroll area. Also check the framework: Vue support sits at v1 while React is on v2, so do not assume the two docs sets match, and remember Tailwind's own Catalyst and shadcn/ui already sit on top of these primitives, so pulling both in duplicates the behaviour layer.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation for 'accessible behaviour, zero opinions about looks' in the Tailwind world, maintained by the Tailwind core team, so it tracks the CSS framework it is meant to pair with.
notable_for: data-attribute state hooks for Tailwind variants
focus trapping, scroll locking, inert backgrounds
